```{r}
#| label: load-libraries

library(ggpubr)
library(stringdist) # fuzzy matches
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
#| label: import-data

mp_sed_con <- read.csv(file = "Data/sed_mp_con.csv")
condition_scores <- read.csv(file = "Data/b23_conditionscores.csv")
benthic_abundance <- read.csv(file = "Data/B23 Post SDR benthic data.csv")
bight_infauna_unified <- read.csv(file = "Data/ed14 historical Bight infauna for unified DB v2.csv")
b23_infauna_summary<- read_excel("Data/B23 appx salinity SQO BLOE output summary.xlsx", sheet = "mambi")

```

```{r}
#| label: mps-x-all-benthic-indicies
mpdata_scores <- left_join(mp_sed_con, condition_scores) |>
```

```{r, M-AMBI}
#| label: mps-x-mambi

ambi <- mpdata_scores |> 
  filter(index == "M-AMBI")

# 1. Normality: Shapiro-Wilk test (p > 0.05 suggests normality)
shapiro.test(ambi$score)
shapiro.test(ambi$n_g_sed_dw) 

# 2. Normality: Q-Q plots
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
qqnorm(ambi$score, main = "Q-Q Plot: score")
qqline(ambi$score, col = "steelblue")
qqnorm(ambi$n_g_sed_dw, main = "Q-Q Plot: n_g_sed_dw")
qqline(ambi$n_g_sed_dw, col = "steelblue")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 3. Linearity: scatter plot with LOESS and linear smoother
ggplot(ambi, aes(x = score, y = n_g_sed_dw)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "steelblue", se = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "tomato", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Linearity check: score vs n_g_sed_dw (M-AMBI)",
       subtitle = "Blue = linear fit, Red dashed = LOESS")

# 4. Outliers: boxplots
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(ambi$score, main = "Outlier check: score")
boxplot(ambi$n_g_sed_dw, main = "Outlier check: n_g_sed_dw")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 5. Spearman's correlation test (all of the Pearson's assumptions violated)
cor.test(ambi$score, ambi$n_g_sed_dw, method = "spearman")

corr <- ambi |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = score, y = n_g_sed_dw))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "steelblue") +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", label.x.npc = "left", label.y.npc = "top") +
  facet_wrap(~index, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "M-AMBI score", y = "")

corr
```

```{r}
#| label: taxon-abundance-correlation
#Join microplastics sediment concentration data with benthic taxon abundance

mpdata_abundance <- left_join(mp_sed_con, benthic_abundance, by = "stationid") |>
  select(-X, -lab.x, -lab.y, -sampledate, -replicate, -voucher, -personalvoucher, -qualifier, -taxonomist )

#Check where data is missing
mpdata_abundance |> 
  filter(is.na(abundance)) |> 
  distinct(stationid) |> 
  nrow()

#21 stations with microplastics data do not have abundance data
#drop stations with no abundance data from analysis

mpdata_abundance <- mpdata_abundance |>
  drop_na(abundance)

#taxon-abundance-correlation

taxon_cor <- mpdata_abundance |>
  group_by(taxon) |>
  filter(n() >= 5) |>
  summarise(
    n_stations = n(),
    spearman_r = cor(abundance, n_g_sed_dw, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    p_value = cor.test(abundance, n_g_sed_dw, method = "spearman")$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(p_value) |>
  as.data.frame()

taxon_sig_neg_cor <- taxon_cor |>
  filter(spearman_r < 0 & p_value < 0.05)

#taxon-correlation-plot

##As expected some species are positively correlated and some are negatively correlated with MP abundance. This on its own isn't very useful. Need to look if species traits or families are positively or negatively correlated

taxon_cor |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "p < 0.05",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    sig = factor(sig, levels = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.01", "p < 0.05", "ns")),
    taxon = reorder(taxon, spearman_r)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = spearman_r, y = taxon, fill = sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "p < 0.001" = "#2166ac",
    "p < 0.01"  = "#74add1",
    "p < 0.05"  = "#abd9e9",
    "ns"        = "grey75"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "Spearman r",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Significance",
    title = "Taxon abundance vs. MP sediment concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


```{r}
#| label: nmds-mps-x-mambi-overlay-families

#From B23 benthic infauna report
# Macrobenthic community composition among the different strata was evaluated using non
# metric Multi-Dimensional Scaling (nMDS) ordination of Bray-Curtis similarity values calculated 
# from presence-absence transformed abundance of all samples. After the ordination, natural 
# environmental factors (% sand, silt, and clay, total organic carbon and total nitrogen content, 
# water depth, latitude, and longitude) and species abundance were correlated to the ordination 
# plot pattern to provide insight into any distribution patterns of samples observed in the 
# ordination (e.g., Gibson et al. 2013). Characteristic species contributing to within-group 
# similarity and distinguishing taxa accounting for the mean Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between 
# sample groupings illustrated in the nMDS were characterized using similarity percentage 
# (SIMPER) analysis (Clarke et al. 2008; Warton et al. 2012). Community analyses were done with 
# the metaMDS (similarity and ordination) and envFit (species and environmental factor 
# correlations) programs within the R Vegan package (v2.7.2 Oksanen et al. 2025 [R version 
# 4.5.2]) or PRIMER v7 (SIMPER analysis) (Clarke et al. 2014).




```



```{r}
#| label: phyla-and-family-analyses

##David mentioned that species traits (e.g., position, mobility, reproduction, feeding) vary at the family level. Join families to the abundance data and analyze

#Check taxon overlap with historical Bight infauna
shared_taxa <- intersect(unique(mpdata_abundance$taxon), unique(bight_infauna_unified$taxon))
only_in_mpdata <- setdiff(unique(mpdata_abundance$taxon), unique(bight_infauna_unified$taxon))

cat("Taxa in both mpdata_abundance and bight_infauna_unified:", length(shared_taxa), "\n")
cat("Taxa only in mpdata (not in historical data):", length(only_in_mpdata), "\n")

#51 taxa in mpdata that don't match with taxa in unified data
##Investigating to see if this is real or if there are syntax issues

ref_taxa <- unique(bight_infauna_unified$taxon)

best_idx <- amatch(only_in_mpdata, ref_taxa, method = "jw", maxDist = 1)

fuzzy_matches <- data.frame(
  mpdata_taxon = only_in_mpdata,
  best_match_infauna_unified   = ref_taxa[best_idx],
  jw_distance  = stringdist(only_in_mpdata, ref_taxa[best_idx], method = "jw")
) |>
  arrange(jw_distance)

# Low distance (~0) = likely a typo/spacing issue; NA best_match = truly no close match
potential_typos <- fuzzy_matches |> filter(!is.na(best_match_infauna_unified))

write.csv(potential_typos, "Data/taxon_syntax.csv", row.names = FALSE)

## There are some matches missing due to (what seem to be(?)) typos. "Fixing" these for downstream analysis
#Created a key for changing some names, BUT probably want DAVID to check these at somepoint and see if others can be matched manually. In the meantime this is probably okay for looking at broad trends

taxon_nomenclature_updates <- read.csv(file = "Data/taxon_nomenclature_updates.csv")

mpdata_abundance <- mpdata_abundance |>
  left_join(taxon_nomenclature_updates, by = c("taxon" = "mpdata_taxon")) |>
  mutate(taxon = coalesce(mpdata_taxon_updated, taxon)) |>
  select(-mpdata_taxon_updated)

taxa_classification <- bight_infauna_unified |> 
  select(taxon, Phylum, Subphylum, Superclass, Class, Subclass, Infraclass, Superorder, Order, Suborder, Infraorder, Superfamily, Family) |> 
  distinct(taxon, Phylum, Subphylum, Superclass, Class, Subclass, Infraclass, Superorder, Order, Suborder, Infraorder, Superfamily, Family)

n_distinct(taxa_classification$taxon)    #2860
n_distinct(mpdata_abundance$taxon)  #787

# for example "B ipalponephtys cornuta" (1)  changed to --> "Bipalponephtys cornuta" (10)
#there are still some records missing classification

mpdata_sp_class <- left_join(mpdata_abundance, taxa_classification, by = "taxon") ##add 


mpdata_sp_class |>
  count(Phylum) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(Phylum, n))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Number of records", y = NULL, title = "Records per Phylum") +
  theme_minimal()

mpdata_sp_phylum <- mpdata_sp_class |> 
  drop_na(Phylum)

phylum_abundance <- mpdata_sp_phylum |>
  group_by(stationid, Phylum, n_g_sed_dw, stratumtype) |>
  summarise(abundance = sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

phylum_cor <- phylum_abundance |>
  group_by(Phylum) |>
  filter(n() >= 5) |>
  summarise(
    n_stations = n(),
    spearman_r = cor(abundance, n_g_sed_dw, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    p_value = cor.test(abundance, n_g_sed_dw, method = "spearman")$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) |>
  arrange(p_adj) |>
  as.data.frame()

phylum_sig_neg_cor <- phylum_cor |>
  filter(spearman_r < 0 & p_value < 0.05)

phylum_n_labels <- phylum_cor |>
  filter(p_value < 0.2) |>
  select(Phylum, n_stations)

phylum_abundance |>
  filter(Phylum %in% phylum_n_labels$Phylum) |>
  left_join(phylum_n_labels, by = "Phylum") |>
  mutate(Phylum = paste0(Phylum, " (n=", n_stations, ")")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = abundance, y = n_g_sed_dw)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "steelblue") +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", label.x.npc = "left", label.y.npc = "top", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~Phylum, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Abundance (log scale)", y = "MP concentration (particles/g dw)", title = "Phylum abundance vs. MP sediment concentration") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)

#phylum-correlation-plot

##As expected some families are positively correlated and some are negatively correlated with MP abundance.

phylum_cor |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "p < 0.05",
      TRUE          ~ "ns"
    ),
    sig = factor(sig, levels = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.01", "p < 0.05", "ns")),
    Phylum = reorder(Phylum, spearman_r)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = spearman_r, y = Phylum, fill = sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "p < 0.001" = "#2166ac",
    "p < 0.01"  = "#74add1",
    "p < 0.05"  = "#abd9e9",
    "ns"        = "grey75"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "Spearman r",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Significance",
    title = "Phylum abundance vs. MP sediment concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
